episodes.title: The Rain Counter
episodes.premise: A night courier finds a kiosk that takes memories as payment for the weather.

panels.scene: Sena cycles downhill through torrents
She finds a dry circle around a glowing kiosk
panels.caption: The rain stopped at the edge of a circle.

panels.scene: Dawa lifts the shutter
panels.dialogue: Dawa: Last purchase of the night.

panels.scene: A brass meter displays a falling droplet
Sena holds out a wet coin
panels.dialogue: Sena: I’ll pay for five dry minutes.

panels.scene: Dawa points to a shelf of bottled memories
panels.dialogue: Dawa: We don’t take money.

panels.scene: Dawa shows a bottle containing a laughing child
panels.dialogue: Dawa: Some people sell the happiest thing they remember.

panels.scene: Sena asks what bought the storm
panels.dialogue: Sena: Then who paid for this?

panels.scene: Dawa reveals a sealed jar with a drawing of a small dog
Sena recognizes her childhood dog from the label
panels.dialogue: Sena: That’s my dog. That’s his crooked ear.

panels.scene: She reaches for it and the clouds bulge
Dawa catches her wrist gently
panels.dialogue: Dawa: Wait. Unpaid weather collects interest.

panels.scene: Sena sees floodwater rising toward a basement window
panels.caption: The river had reached the basement windows.

panels.scene: A child inside bangs on the glass
Dawa sets the jar on a brass scale
panels.dialogue: Dawa: A memory for a memory. That’s the rule.

panels.scene: The scale demands a new memory to free the old one
Sena recalls her dog waiting on the doorstep
panels.caption: Every evening, he waited at the door.

panels.scene: She looks from the memory to the trapped child
panels.dialogue: Sena: You can have the face in that window.

panels.scene: Sena puts a fresh memory of the child's face on the scale
The old jar opens, but the rain grows fiercer
panels.caption: The kiosk had promised her one thing and taken another.

panels.scene: Sena notices an empty switch marked with a sun icon
She lifts both jars off the scale at once
panels.dialogue: Sena: Take your hands off the scale.

panels.scene: Dawa pulls the sun lever
panels.dialogue: Dawa: I haven’t done this in years.

panels.scene: The weather meter cracks into a spray of gold
panels.caption: Finally, the rain ran out of things to say.

panels.scene: Sena and Dawa pull the child out of the basement
panels.dialogue: Sena: Hold on. I’ve got you.

panels.scene: The child runs to a relieved parent
Dawa opens the kiosk windows and lets bottled memories fly
panels.dialogue: Dawa: If they come looking, tell them the shop is closed.

panels.scene: In morning light Sena finds the old dog's collar in her bag
She cannot remember the child's face but recognizes their little yellow umbrella
panels.caption: She remembered the umbrella. She remembered what she had done.

panels.scene: Sena cycles home behind the umbrella as the sun breaks through
panels.caption: That turned out to be enough.

panels.scene: Sena returns to a weather kiosk where the child she rescued waits under a yellow umbrella
panels.dialogue: Sena: You came back.

panels.scene: The child sets a brass dog tag on the kiosk counter
panels.dialogue: Child: I found it in the water.

panels.scene: Close-up of a rusty brass tag in Sena’s hand
panels.caption: She knew its shape before she remembered the name.

panels.scene: Dawa opens a drawer full of old receipts and offers one
panels.dialogue: Dawa: This one was your mother’s.

panels.scene: Golden flashback of a tired mother, small daughter, and crooked-eared dog huddled on a doorstep
panels.caption: The morning after the hardest night.

panels.scene: Sena studies a cabinet of storm clouds trapped in jars
panels.dialogue: Sena: Let’s give the city its weather back.

panels.scene: Sena props the kiosk door open with her bicycle as the child raises the yellow umbrella
panels.dialogue: Child: What if it rains again?

panels.scene: Dawa hands Sena a brass key
panels.dialogue: Dawa: Then we’ll open a window.

panels.scene: Sena unlocks a tall glass cabinet and tiny storm clouds pour out
Neighbors shelter together under colorful umbrellas in a sunshower
panels.caption: It was the first rain nobody owed for.

panels.scene: The child paints a crooked-eared dog on the kiosk shutter while Sena ties the tag to her handlebars
panels.dialogue: Child: What should I call him?

panels.scene: Sena cycles away past the painted dog while Dawa serves tea to neighbors
panels.dialogue: Sena: Call him Lucky.

episodes.title: Moon Laundry
episodes.premise: A laundromat attendant discovers a customer has been washing the moon to erase a last goodbye.

panels.scene: Ari folds towels under fluorescent lights at midnight
panels.caption: The laundromat stayed open for people whose days ran long.

panels.scene: Min enters carrying a linen bag that floats
He pulls a tiny glowing crescent out of his bag
panels.dialogue: Ari: Is that the moon?

panels.scene: He loads the crescent into a washing machine
panels.dialogue: Min: Gentle cycle.

panels.scene: Ari leans close as stars appear behind the glass
A shadow on the moon takes the shape of a hand waving goodbye
panels.caption: The same hand had been waving since he came in.

panels.scene: Min pours detergent with trembling fingers
panels.dialogue: Ari: You’ve washed it before.

panels.scene: Ari notices the same handprint on his coat sleeve
Min opens a photo wallet showing his smiling adult sister
panels.dialogue: Min: My sister. Her last trip home.

panels.scene: The washing machine turns the moon to a full bright disk
Min's reflection smiles but his face does not
panels.caption: The reflection could pretend. Min couldn’t.

panels.scene: Ari reaches for the power switch before he can wash again
panels.dialogue: Ari: Let it stop for a minute.

panels.scene: Min tries to explain beside the still machine
panels.dialogue: Min: I wanted that night to hurt less.

panels.scene: Flashback: his sister waves from a late-night bus
Flashback: Min watches the bus leave without waving back
panels.caption: He used to think he would catch the next bus.

panels.scene: Present: Min stares at an empty bus stop across the street
Ari retrieves a spare sock from a lost-property basket
panels.dialogue: Ari: I keep the singles. People come back for them.

panels.scene: She compares the lost sock to the moon beside its matching half
panels.dialogue: Ari: Sometimes they only want to know where they went.

panels.scene: Ari puts the damp moon on the counter
Min presses his hand beside the handprint
panels.caption: His hand fit the space beside hers.

panels.scene: Ari opens the laundromat door to the cold night
Min raises his hand toward the sky beside her
panels.dialogue: Min: Hi, sis.

panels.scene: The shadow hand rises on the moon's surface to meet his silhouette
Min smiles and opens the window above the dryer
panels.caption: The window stuck, then gave.

panels.scene: The glowing moon drifts upward out the window
Ari and Min watch it grow in the sky
panels.caption: By the time it reached the roofs, it was the size a moon ought to be.

panels.scene: Min slips the photo back into his wallet with a softer expression
Ari hangs the misplaced sock on a clothesline
panels.caption: Somewhere a sock was waiting to be found.

panels.scene: Min sets two hot drinks on the folding table
panels.dialogue: Min: Tea? I got two.

panels.scene: Wide dawn view of the two in the laundromat under a faint full moon
panels.caption: Neither of them checked the time.

panels.scene: Morning light in the laundromat, Min finds an old luminous bus ticket beside his tea
panels.dialogue: Min: I thought I threw that away.

panels.scene: Ari looks across the street at a parked city bus
panels.dialogue: Ari: You could try the next one.

panels.scene: Min walks across the street with the ticket and a photo of his sister
panels.caption: His feet remembered the stop.

panels.scene: An elderly woman bus driver opens the door and recognizes Min
panels.dialogue: Driver: You’re her brother.

panels.scene: The driver offers a folded yellow scarf from a box behind her seat
panels.dialogue: Driver: She left it on the back seat.

panels.scene: Min sits alone in the parked bus with the scarf on his lap
panels.dialogue: Min: I thought the wave was all I had left.

panels.scene: Min looks down at the scarf, beside a moon reflection on the empty seat
Back at the laundromat, Ari finds a striped sock in the lost-property basket
panels.dialogue: Ari: Well, look who showed up.

panels.scene: Min returns to the laundromat holding the yellow scarf
panels.dialogue: Min: Could you show me how to wash this?

panels.scene: They handwash the scarf in a basin with faint stars reflected in the water
panels.dialogue: Ari: Cold water. Give it time.

panels.scene: Min pins the scarf beside two matching socks in morning light
panels.caption: Some things came back in pairs.

panels.scene: Ari turns the shop sign as Min leaves wearing the scarf under a pale full moon
panels.caption: Some things just needed a place to dry.

episodes.title: The Last Exit
episodes.premise: A maintenance worker discovers an evacuation train that cannot leave until one forgotten passenger is found.

panels.scene: Jo stands alone at an underground station under emergency lights
panels.caption: The last exit was due to seal at dawn.

panels.scene: She kneels to repair a blinking floor sign
A silver evacuation train slides in silently
panels.caption: The evacuation train arrived without a sound.

panels.scene: Kei leans out and checks a punched paper roster
panels.dialogue: Kei: We’re one short.

panels.scene: Jo shows him a clean empty platform
panels.dialogue: Jo: I cleared the station myself.

panels.scene: The last carriage door blinks one red light
Kei and Jo enter the empty carriage
panels.dialogue: Jo: Empty.

panels.scene: A passenger count display shows a single missing silhouette
panels.dialogue: Kei: The train disagrees.

panels.scene: Jo follows tiny paw prints beside the seats
She finds a chewed cable below a bench
panels.caption: Something had been chewing on the platform sensors.

panels.scene: Kei lifts a colorful photograph of an old station cat from a display
panels.caption: The station’s oldest employee had never punched a card.

panels.scene: Jo hears a scratching sound from behind the timetable
Jo pulls the timetable aside and finds a tiny speaker
panels.dialogue: Jo: The speaker is picking up the office vent.

panels.scene: Kei checks a wall clock as the water alarm turns red
panels.dialogue: Kei: We have two minutes.

panels.scene: In a distant station office a white cat with one black ear paws at a vent
Jo follows cables to a lowering floodgate
panels.caption: The floodgate began to lower.

panels.scene: Kei wedges his conductor bag under the floodgate
panels.dialogue: Kei: Go. I’ll hold it as long as the bag lasts.

panels.scene: Jo crawls underneath toward the office
Jo sees the white cat trapped behind bent vent bars
panels.dialogue: Jo: So this is where you’ve been sleeping.

panels.scene: She takes a bolt cutter off her red utility belt
The cat backs away as sparks flash from a nearby cable
panels.caption: The cat pressed back against the vent wall.

panels.scene: Jo offers its favorite toy mouse from the office desk
panels.dialogue: Jo: Remember this?

panels.scene: The cat puts one paw through the opening
panels.caption: One paw. Then another.

panels.scene: Jo scoops the cat up as the floodgate crushes the bag
Jo passes the cat up through a service hatch to Kei
panels.dialogue: Jo: Passenger for you!

panels.scene: Kei pulls Jo onto the platform as water fills the tunnel
panels.dialogue: Kei: I count two.

panels.scene: Jo and Kei hurry onboard with the cat
The red passenger silhouette finally turns green
panels.caption: For the first time that night, the door turned green.

panels.scene: The train emerges above ground into sunrise
Jo sits beside Kei with the cat asleep on the paper roster
panels.caption: The passenger slept straight through arrival.

panels.scene: Silver train stops in a sunny depot. White cat yawns on Kei’s roster
panels.dialogue: Kei: End of the line.

panels.scene: Jo examines the cat’s service tag engraved with an antenna symbol
panels.dialogue: Jo: This isn’t a name tag.

panels.scene: The cat leaps from the train and runs to a silent emergency radio console
Jo kneels by the console and sees a single red fault light
panels.dialogue: Jo: The relay never sent the all-clear.

panels.scene: Kei spots a rescue locomotive approaching on distant tracks
panels.dialogue: Kei: They’re about to take the tunnel.

panels.scene: Jo touches the dead transmit button while the cat taps at a loose cable
panels.dialogue: Jo: Show me what you were chewing.

panels.scene: Jo pulls a copper cable from the maintenance cabinet
panels.dialogue: Kei: How long do you need?

panels.scene: Kei runs to a semaphore lever as the rescue locomotive approaches
panels.dialogue: Jo: Buy me ten seconds.

panels.scene: Jo repairs the console with gloved hands while the white cat watches
The depot signal goes red and a rescue locomotive brakes outside the flooded tunnel
panels.dialogue: Kei: They saw it.

panels.scene: A rescue worker offers Jo a tiny reflective station badge for the white cat
panels.dialogue: Rescue worker: Does your colleague have a name?

panels.scene: Jo clips the small badge onto the cat while Kei puts down the roster beside a bowl of water
panels.dialogue: Jo: Put down ‘Conductor.’

episodes.title: The Cartographer of Missing Streets
episodes.premise: Episode 01: Undeliverable. A courier discovers that a missing bridge has arrived in her delivery basket.

panels.scene: Ika brakes her bicycle at a vanished bridge on a rainy city river.
panels.caption: At 6:14, Bridge Street disappeared.

panels.scene: Close-up of Ika in her orange rain jacket.
panels.dialogue: That is going to make me late.

panels.scene: A tiny glowing streetlamp emerges from the parcel in her basket.
panels.dialogue: Please do not mark me undeliverable.

panels.scene: Ika opens the parcel beneath a bakery awning.
panels.dialogue: Who ordered a talking bridge? Someone who remembers where I belong.

panels.scene: The delivery label reads HOME.
panels.dialogue: There is no house there anymore.

panels.scene: Inside the parcel, a glowing miniature road leads to a blue door.
panels.dialogue: A house is not the same thing as a way home.

panels.scene: Ika pedals over a luminous bridge forming beneath her wheels toward a portal.
panels.caption: To be continued.
panels.dialogue: Fine. But you are signing for this.
